title: Instagram’s ‘First Draft’ feature aims to make editing Reels less tedious
slides: Why is Instagram's new feature just called 'First Draft'?
It auto-saves unfinished Reels for later editing.
You can't share drafts directly—they're hidden by default.
This means planning content timelines gets much easier.
Try it now: start a reel, save, and revisit tomorrow.
thread_text:
1. Hidden by default

Instagram's new 'First Draft' feature auto-saves unfinished Reels, but they're invisible to your followers until you choose to publish.

2. Not for sharing

You can't share drafts directly—instead, they're stored privately, giving you a safe space to experiment without public pressure.

3. Planning made easy

This hidden layer lets you map out content timelines, batch-create reels, and revisit them anytime before going live.

4. The twist

First Draft doesn't notify your audience or clutter their feed—your unfinished work stays yours until it's ready for prime time.

5. Try it now

Start a reel today, save it as a draft, and revisit it tomorrow with fresh eyes. Will you see the flaws you missed?

instagram.caption:
Your unfinished Reels are about to get a private hiding spot. Instagram’s new “First Draft” feature auto-saves your half-finished videos without showing them to anyone.

Drafts stay invisible by default. You can’t share them directly, so there’s zero pressure while you experiment. Batch-create content and revisit it later with fresh eyes before publishing.

For creators, this kills the “post it before it’s ready” panic. You build your timeline quietly, then release when it actually works.

Open the app right now, start a Reel, save it as a draft, and check it tomorrow. What’s the first flaw you’ll spot? 🎬📝🙈
